subject: Post-call synthesis + POC initiation plan — SkyQuest Labs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.p@skyquestlabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call synthesis + POC initiation plan — SkyQuest Labs

Thanks again for the call earlier, Maya — great context. I wanted to capture the highlights and propose a short, pragmatic POC plan we can execute in the next 4–6 weeks. High level: you want to validate production latency/cost at scale for the contextual search and chat features in your analyst UI, plus confirm safety filters and access controls.

Key pains you emphasized:
- Slow conversational responses during peak reporting periods (users see 500–800ms average, spikes >1.5s).
- Cost unpredictability when end-users run long-context searches across proprietary docs.
- Auditability/access: security team requires evidence of request logs and a path to deploy inside their VPC for PHI data.

Success criteria (agreed candidate):
- P99 latency for median query profile < 220ms end-to-end for the chat endpoint;
- Cost forecast showing >=30% reduction in token cost per useful response vs current baseline;
- Ability to ingest a 2M-token sample data slice and run prompt-set evals with redactions in place;
- Delivery of a short security artifacts pack for their InfoSec review (encrypted logs, KMS config).

Proposed POC scope (4–6 weeks):
Week 0 (this week): finalize data access + sign-off on scope.
Week 1: environment provisioning (dedicated sandbox on Redwood Dedicated + access allowlist).
Week 2–3: ingest sample corpus, run prompt/eval set, baseline performance.
Week 4: run burst tests (simulated peak load), iterate quantization/batching settings.
Week 5–6: produce POC report (latency/cost tradeoffs), security artifacts, and next-steps recommendation.

Immediate asks from SkyQuest:
1) Provide a 2GB sample slice (or S3 path) and a contact for network allowlist.
2) InfoSec point-of-contact for the artifacts checklist.
3) Two example user flows you want prioritized for prompt/eval (search -> refine -> summarize; analyst chat).

Attachments: I attached a lightweight POC charter and a sample manifest template for the data slice.

Next steps: Maya — if this looks right, can you confirm the S3 path and InfoSec contact by Friday? We’ll produce a signed POC charter (attached) and kick off provisioning once you confirm.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Maya Patel <maya.p@skyquestlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis + POC initiation plan — SkyQuest Labs

Thanks, Soojin — this is exactly the kind of plan we want. Quick confirmations:
- I can drop a 2GB sample (redacted) into the S3 bucket this week; uploading will be done by Thu EOD.
- InfoSec contact: Daniel Cho (daniel.cho@skyquestlabs.com) — he’ll be on the thread once we have the charter.
- Priority user flows: 1) Analyst search + summary; 2) Chat-assisted extraction for regulatory snippets.

Couple of clarifying Qs:
1) For the burst tests, what RPS target should we expect for the simulation?
2) Will data remain inside our VPC for the POC or will you pull into a Redwood-managed sandbox?

I’ll attach the S3 manifest and loop Daniel after the charter is signed.

—
Maya Patel
Head of Product | SkyQuest Labs
maya.p@skyquestlabs.com | +1 (206) 555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.p@skyquestlabs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis + POC initiation plan — SkyQuest Labs

Great notes — answering Maya’s questions and listing technical access items.

Burst test target: we recommend starting with a 200 RPS synthetic burst (95th percentile concurrent users for your plan) then stress to 500 RPS for 30s windows to observe tail latency behavior. We’ll produce a gradated test plan so we don’t overprovision.

Data residency for POC: two options (both viable):
A) Redwood Dedicated sandbox in our secure tenancy (logs and artifacts exported encrypted to your S3);
B) Private deployment inside your VPC using our Private package (best for PHI/regulatory data but adds ~1-week provisioning overhead).

For either path we’ll need the following to start provisioning:
- S3 path with read-only test credentials (or a presigned upload) and a small manifest (we’ve included a manifest template).
- IP allowlist block(s) (we provided a sample workbook).
- IAM/service account for our ingestion agent (least privilege: read-only list/get on the sample prefix).
- If you choose VPC deploy: CIDR for peering and preferred region.

I’m attaching a minimal infra checklist (network-allowlist-template.xlsx) and a draft set of prompt evals we’ll run against the sample. Sergio, can you prepare the initial quantization/ batching hypothesis so we can test cost/latency tradeoffs in week 2?

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis + POC initiation plan — SkyQuest Labs

Thanks, Maya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Daniel (cc) would be great to have on the next note.

Action items we’ll take this week:
- Redwood: provision Dedicated sandbox and create presigned URL for dataset upload (Soojin) — target Thu EOD.
- Redwood: run a short baseline on small sample and share initial latency/cost snapshot (Karthik + Sergio) — target Mon next week.
- SkyQuest: upload the sample to the presigned URL and confirm Daniel as InfoSec contact (Maya) — target Thu EOD.

If we get those things in place on schedule, we’ll begin week-1 provisioning Monday and aim to have baseline results by the end of week 2.

Thanks all — excited to move this forward.

—
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
